news.title: Internationals: Kavuma-McQueen nets winner
news.body_en: Calvin Diakite, Jashayde Greenwood and Gabriel Sambou all started for England Under-18s while Ryan Kavuma-McQueen came off the bench to net a late winner as the Young Lions defeated South Korea 2-1 on Wednesday morning. Kavuma-McQueen, who is currently on loan at Portsmouth from Chelsea, scored the decisive goal in the first minute of additional time, his looping shot finding the top corner. The winger had been introduced on the hour, shortly after England had taken the lead, and at the same time Diakite and Greenwood were withdrawn. The victory means Will Antwi’s squad have progressed to the UEFA Friendship Cup semi-final, having maintained their 100 per cent record to top Group A. They will now face the winner of Group B on Sunday. Scotland Under-19’s were also in action, as Alfie Osborne featured for the full 90 minutes in a 2-0 loss to Ukraine. The 17-year-old played every minute of Scotland's Spanish tour, which concluded this morning.

news.title: Ultimate Goal of the Season: Group D results
news.body_en: The results are in and we can now confirm the final two Chelsea players to progress to the quarter-finals of our Ultimate Goal of the Season competition. The fourth and final group contained several spectacular strikes spanning 15 years of action, and in the end it was goals scored by Eden Hazard and Moises Caicedo that you voted the best of the bunch on the Chelsea Official App. Hazard’s was that spectacular solo strike at Anfield that lingers long in the memory, with the brilliant Belgian weaving between several Liverpool players before finishing in style in front of the travelling support. Caicedo’s goal that progressed was no less spectacular, a perfect strike from the halfway line that dropped into the net after Bournemouth’s keeper was caught out of position. It was some way for Moises to open his Blues account! Hazard and Caicedo beat off competition from fellow Goal of the Season winners Ashley Cole (2010), Lewis Baker (2014) and Mateo Kovacic (2022). The quarter-final line-up is now complete and tomorrow (Thursday) we will reveal who is facing who in the knockout stage, with Caicedo (2024) and Hazard (with three selections for 2016, 2017 and 2019) joined by Ramires (2012), Michael Essien (both 2007 and 2009) and Joao Pedro (2026).

news.title: French Connection: The shared history between Chelsea Women and Lyon
news.body_en: Our Women's Champions League trip to face Lyon tonight will bring together a remarkable array of connections between the two clubs. Kick-off is at 8pm UK time, with Sonia Bompastor preparing to return to the club where she established herself as one of the most successful figures in the history of the women's game. The Chelsea head coach is far from the only member of our squad and staff with strong links to OL Lyonnes. Assistant coach Camille Abily spent five years working alongside Bompastor on the Lyon coaching staff after her glittering playing career with the French club. Kadeisha Buchanan, Lucy Bronze, Ellie Carpenter and Melvine Malard have all worn the Lyon shirt, while each has their own story to tell about their time in France. It means Wednesday's fixture is about much more than simply two of the biggest clubs in the Women's Champions League meeting again, but a clash between two clubs with so much shared history. For Bompastor, this will be a return to a club that has played such a huge part in her life. She spent two spells as a player at Lyon, from 2006 to 2009 and again from 2010 to 2013, winning six league titles, three French Cups and back-to-back Champions Leagues in 2011 and 2012. After hanging up her boots, she remained at the club, managing the academy for eight years before taking charge of the first team in 2021. Lifting three league titles, she added a French Cup and another Champions League trophy to her collection. In the process, she became the first person to win the Women's Champions League as both a player and a head coach. And Bompastor admits returning to her former club will be a special occasion. ‘It will be an emotional game for me individually, even if the game won't be around me,’ she said. 'The most important thing is for me to prepare the team to perform at their best in that game, but of course it's really a nice thing to just go back to Lyon and play them. They have a really good team, and it will be a great game to see where we are.’ There is also a special connection in the dugout alongside her. Abily was Bompastor's long-time team-mate before eventually becoming her assistant at Lyon, with the pair continuing their partnership when they moved to Chelsea in the summer of 2024. Abily spent five years as an assistant at Lyon and was part of the coaching team that won three league titles and the 2022 Champions League. As a player, Abily won five Champions League titles with Lyon and made more than 150 appearances for France, making her one of the most decorated figures to have crossed the touchline into the Chelsea dugout. Bompastor and Abily are joined by four current Chelsea players who know Lyon particularly well. Bronze spent three seasons in France, winning the Champions League in each campaign, before adding two more Champions League titles during her spell in Spain with Barcelona and signing for Chelsea in 2024. Here, she was reunited with both Bompastor and Abily, having previously played alongside the latter at Lyon. Buchanan's Lyon career lasted five-and-a-half years before she joined Chelsea in 2022, during which she won five Champions League titles and eight domestic trophies. She has since become a mainstay at the heart of the Blues' defence. The defender worked together with Bompastor during the coach's first season in charge of Lyon's senior side. Carpenter is another Chelsea player with strong ties to Lyon. The Australian spent five seasons in France, winning two Champions League trophies and four league titles before moving to London. She was reunited with Malard at Chelsea, having previously played alongside the forward under Bompastor and Abily at Lyon. ‘Obviously we have that relationship from Lyon,’ Carpenter said of Malard. ‘So it's nice to have her on the team.’ For Malard, however, the connection with Bompastor goes back much further. The head coach was instrumental in bringing the forward to Lyon at the age of 14, recognising her talent and helping her to pursue her ambitions in football. ‘Sonia has been so influential, for me and for my family,’ Malard explained. ‘If Sonia had not called my Mum and taken me to Lyon, I would not be here today. She did so much for me when I was at Lyon.’ Now, the pair will return to France together, with Bompastor heading back to the club where she made so much of her history and Malard returning to the place where her own professional journey began. Chelsea and Lyon have met in the Women's Champions League knockout stages twice before, with both ties producing memories that remain firmly etched into the history of this fixture. Lyon won the first leg 2-1 in France, with Erin Cuthbert scoring for Chelsea, before the return at Kingsmeadow ended 1-1 in a dramatic match that saw Chelsea pepper the Lyon goal, hitting the woodwork and missing several chances to take the game to penalties. The enthralling tie ended with Lyon progressing 3-2 on aggregate and ultimately towards another European title. The Blues travelled to Lyon for the first leg, and came away with a famous 1-0 victory thanks to Guro Reiten's fabulous strike. What followed in the second leg at Stamford Bridge has gone down as one of the most dramatic nights in our history. Lyon overturned Chelsea's advantage through goals from Vanessa Gilles and Sara Dabritz, taking a 2-0 lead on the night and 2-1 in the tie. But with the final kick of extra-time, Maren Mjelde held her nerve to convert a penalty to level the aggregate score. Ann-Katrin Berger then became the hero in the shoot-out, saving from Wendie Renard and Lindsey Horan as Chelsea prevailed 4-3 on penalties. Now, more than three years later, the two clubs meet again. Bompastor will walk back into a stadium where she made so much history. Abily will return to the club where she first forged her coaching partnership with the Chelsea boss. Bronze, Buchanan, Carpenter and Malard will face former team-mates. But once the whistle goes, all of those connections will be put to one side. Another chapter in the Chelsea-Lyon story is about to be written.

news.title: Chelsea youngsters called up by England Women youth teams
news.body_en: Chelsea's Nelly Las has been called up to the England Women's Under-23 side ahead of the forthcoming international break, while a trio have been named in the Under-19 squad. The 18-year-old joined Chelsea from Leicester City on a four-year contract in July and made her Blues debut as a second-half substitute during our 1-0 victory away at Real Sociedad earlier in the campaign. The attacking full-back also came off the bench in our 5-0 win at Manchester United on 13 September. The young Lionesses will play against Norway at York City's LNER Community Stadium on Monday 12 October at 7.30pm. The fixture will mark the start of England’s defence of the U23 European Competition title, which they won in April with a 3-0 victory over Sweden in the final. For the 2026/27 campaign, England have been drawn in Group B alongside Norway, Belgium, Portugal and Italy. 'I’m really excited to get the staff and players together for the new season,' said head coach Lydia Bedford. 'It’s going to be an important year for the Under-23s, particularly with a senior World Cup on the horizon, and we want to keep pushing the players and helping them take the next steps in their development. Meanwhile, three Blues have been called to the England Women's Under-19 squad for a triple-header of qualifiers for the 2027 Women's U19 European Championships to be played in Bosnia during the October international break. Chelsea Academy Under-18s Elise Christian and Gabriella Storey have been selected, as has Lois Shooter, who is currently on loan at Nottingham Forest in WSL2. England will play against Denmark at 12pm on Wednesday 7 October, followed by a match against Switzerland on Saturday 10 October, also at 12pm. The third match will be against Bosnia & Herzegovina at 12pm on Tuesday 13 October.

Chelsea welcomes Topps as Official Trading Card Partner
news.body_en: Chelsea Football Club and Chelsea FC Women today announce the expansion of our relationship with Topps, which becomes Official Trading Card Partner of the club on a long-term, exclusive deal. The new partnership includes trading cards, trading card games and stickers for the Topps, Match Attax and Merlin brands. Marking the continuation of a successful collaboration that began in 2018, rooted in creativity, fandom and a shared passion for collecting, the partnership brings the magic of collecting even closer to Chelsea supporters. For fans, it means a closer connection to the moments and history that define Chelsea, with collectibles built around the players and teams they love. To celebrate, Topps met with Levi Colwill, Nathalie Bjorn, Pedro Neto and Sjoeke Nusken to discuss collecting and to chase some of their teammates as they open packs together. The new agreement is exclusive at club level and folds in more player autographs and game-worn relics for fans to chase. It also brings expanded products capturing Chelsea FC Women, further increasing the team's visibility and growing our community of passionate fans. For Chelsea fans and collectors alike, that means access to more premium, first-of-a-kind trading cards and more collectibles than ever before.

Internationals: Rogers helps England to victory as young Blue scores
news.body_en: Morgan Rogers helped England secure their first Nations League win of the new campaign with a 2-0 victory over Czechia, while Chelsea striker Shim Mheuka found the net as our young Blues enjoyed a successful day on international duty. Rogers came into Thomas Tuchel’s starting XI at the Fortuna Arena in Prague and was involved in the move which led to Harry Kane’s second-half goal, after Anthony Gordon had opened the scoring. Our attacking midfielder went close to breaking the deadlock himself around a quarter of an hour into the contest, turning inside the penalty area and curling an effort against the far post. Elliot Anderson and Bukayo Saka's follow-ups were then blocked. Czechia were then reduced to 10 men when Pavel Sulc was dismissed following a VAR review of his challenge on Anderson, although England had to wait until the second half to take the lead. Gordon headed home Trent Alexander-Arnold’s fine cross shortly after the restart, before Rogers helped England double their advantage in the 69th minute. His involvement inside the penalty area left the ball loose for Kane, who finished low into the corner. The Three Lions next travel to Croatia on Saturday, before hosting Czechia at Wembley on Tuesday. Earlier in the day, Mheuka produce a moment of magic to open the scoring as England Under-20s defeated France 2-1 in Spain, with fellow Blue Jesse Derry also featuring. Our striker, currently on loan at Celtic, needed just nine minutes to make his mark, controlling goalkeeper Oliver Whatmuff’s long pass superbly with his chest just inside the France half before driving forward and finishing past Mathys Niflore from outside the area. Mikey Moore then doubled England’s advantage five minutes later before another Blue out on loan, Derry, who is spending the season at Sporting CP, replaced Shea Lacey in the 59th minute. Mheuka was substituted after 74 minutes and Prosper Peter pulled one back for France, but England held on to secure a second successive U20 Euro Elite League victory. They next face Germany on Saturday. Chizaram Ezenwata and Reggie Walsh both came off the bench as England Under-19s recorded a 2-1 victory over Norway in Marbella. The Chelsea pair were introduced in the 70th minute, with Ezenwata replacing Alejandro Rodriguez and Walsh, currently on loan at Wigan Athletic, taking over from Luca Williams-Barnett. Williams-Barnett and Rodriguez had established a two-goal lead before the interval, with Norway halving the deficit shortly after the restart. Goalkeeper Freddy Bernal was an unused substitute as England saw out the win ahead of Friday’s meeting with the United States. Alfie Osborne will be hoping to feature for Scotland Under-19s when they conclude their series of friendlies in Spain against Ukraine tomorrow. The match in La Nucia kicks off at 10am UK time. Calvin Diakite, Jashayde Greenwood and Gabriel Sambou could also be involved when England Under-18s face Korea Republic in the UEFA Friendship Cup in Nyon, Switzerland, at the same time. All three Blues are in Will Antwi’s squad, with that fixture completing England’s group-stage programme before a final placement match on Saturday.

news.title: Key talking points from Sonia Bompastor's pre-Lyon press conference
news.body_en: Sonia Bompastor and Lucy Bronze faced the media at the Parc Olympique Lyonnais on Tuesday evening ahead of their return to face their former side in the Women's Champions League. Here are the stand-out talking points from the press conference... Bompastor represented Lyon as a player before spending eight years in charge of their women's academy side after hanging up her boots. She was then promoted to head coach in 2021, and spent three further years in charge before moving to Chelsea in summer 2024. This is the first time that our head coach has returned to face her former side since her move to England, and there were inevitably questions from the French media on how she is feeling ahead of Wednesday's match. Bronze spent three years at the club between 2017 and 2020. She was asked about playing under legendary French defender Wendie Renard, who has represented Lyon since 2006. Sonia Bompastor: 'It will be full of emotion; that’s obvious.  I’m not the only one on the staff or in this group of players - there are quite a few people who have played or coached here, in this great stadium. 'But there is a match to be played, and that’s the most important thing. My task will be to focus on the preparations and to make sure that my team arrives ready for the match.' 'No, not necessarily. I always want to do well. It doesn't matter what game it is. We've just come off another big game against Arsenal, and we want to shine, to win. 'Yes, this is a special moment, maybe a bit more charged with emotions, but we know how to detach ourselves from that; it’s part of our job. Emotionally and mentally, we know how to prepare so that the match remains the most important thing tomorrow.' 'I have a blast every day being the head coach at Chelsea. Football in England is cultural. It's a culture that is very different from what we have here in France. The Women's Super League is very competitive. 'It was a personal choice to take on this role, because I wanted to challenge myself. I have that chance every weekend in the league, but also in the Champions League. I have the chance to work at a very high-level club at Chelsea. It's a big brand, a big club. I am very happy here, and I take a lot of pleasure from working with this group of players every day.' 'Chelsea are a club with ambitions. So we always build a squad that can compete to win every trophy, especially the Champions League. It's the only one that's missing from the club. 'You have to find the right balance between experienced players and young talent. And then this competition is becoming more and more difficult. There are a lot of clubs now investing in women's football, and sometimes you need a bit of luck to help tip things in the right direction. 'We are not far away. I think we have a team full of quality, a team with a lot of talent, and so we have to approach matches one by one, and also have the mentality to be very competitive. We approach matches with this killer spirit against big opponents.' Lucy Bronze: 'I spent three years at Lyon with Wendie as my captain, and I tell everyone she's the best captain I've ever played under. She's a great player and a great person. I learned so much from her in terms of how she defended her team, how she stood up for people, and the respect that she gained from everyone by doing the right things. 'There are so many words I could use to describe Wendie Renard. I took a lot of the experience that she brought to Lyon, and I try to bring that to Chelsea in terms of leading by example, bringing everyone along with me, and always having the highest standards.'

news.title: Leo Black signs for Chelsea
news.body_en: Chelsea Football Club is pleased to announce the signing of Leo Black, who joins the Blues until 2028 following a successful trial. Black, 20, is a versatile player who can play full-back and midfield, and has represented England at Under-18 and Under-19 levels. In August, Black made his debut for Chelsea Cobham Next Gen in our 5-4 win against West Ham. He also scored in our victories against Arsenal and Fulham before the international break. For his impressive performances, Black was nominated for the PL2 Player of the Month for September 2026.

news.title: Internationals: Estevao Willian features in Brazil comeback
news.body_en: Blues forward Estevao Willian was a second-half substitute as the Selecao ran out 4-2 winners in an entertaining contest against Australia in Brisbane. Brazil were held to a 1-1 draw with Australia last week in the first of a double-header between the countries over this international break, but our former manager Carlo Ancelotti led his side to a comfortable win in the second clash between the pair. Estevao's Brazil took the lead inside the opening three minutes thanks to an effort from Vanderson before the Socceroos fought back to go 2-1 up after 34 minutes with goals from Alessandro Circati and Connor Metcalfe. That was until Raphinha drew the visitors level from the penalty spot on the stroke of half-time. After the break, Ancelotti made several changes, including introducing Estevao in the 61st minute as a replacement on the right side of attack for Bournemouth's Rayan. Estevao looked bright during his 30 minutes of action, showing some flashes of brilliance on the ball and came close to getting his name on the scoresheet with a left-footed effort that narrowly went over the bar. Brazil went on to win the match through a Bruno Guimaraes strike and a Vinicius Junior penalty as their superior quality and strength from the bench shone through. The 19-year-old could be in action once again on Saturday when Brazil head to Kolkata to take on India in an international friendly, with kick-off set for 2pm (UK time).

news.title: Matchday Unseen | Arsenal 🎥
Lucy Bronze excited for Lyon reunion as Chelsea prepare for another big test
news.body_en: Lucy Bronze is relishing the chance to return to her former club as we prepare to face another match against top-level opposition on Wednesday evening. The defender spent a hugely successful spell with the French club and will return to familiar surroundings in the Women's Champions League as one of four Chelsea players with previous connections to Lyon. Bronze was delighted to come through Sunday's hard-fought victory over Arsenal with three points, but her attention has already turned towards our next major test. ‘It was a well-earned three points,’ Bronze said. ‘The game kind of went Arsenal's way in the first half, then we stepped it up in the second, and they threw the kitchen sink at us in the end. It was an entertaining game for the fans. It was a really challenging game to play in, but ultimately I was so happy with the three points. It puts us in a great position near the top of the table.’ The full-back has made no secret of her love for playing in the biggest matches, and Lucy is enjoying the prospect of continuing to test herself against Europe's elite with another round of Champions League fixtures in her sights. ‘It's great. I love playing in the big games, the challenging games,’ she added. ‘That's what the best players in the world want to do. They want to play for the best teams, to be able to compete for trophies, to compete in the league. ‘That's exactly what we're doing this season. We're pushing ourselves in every single game to be able to compete and win every trophy we can.’ After securing a hard-fought 1-0 win in the opening match of our Champions League campaign, the Blues are preparing to capitalise on the three points already earned in the competition's league phase. The match will see Chelsea head coach Sonia Bompastor and her assistant, Camille Abily, return to face their former side, and Bronze is already up for the challenge. ‘It's so exciting,’ Bronze said. ‘My time at Lyon was amazing. All the girls, Ellie (Carpenter), Keish (Kadeisha Buchanan) and Melvine (Malard) had a great time at Lyon, and we all actually played there together as well. ‘We're excited to go there, to be focused on the Champions League, and we know what pedigree Lyon have in the Champions League. To go toe to toe with another team who's one of the best in the world and test ourselves and prove ourselves is going to be exciting.’ Bronze's focus is firmly on Wednesday's Champions League trip to Lyon, before Chelsea return to domestic action away at West Ham United at the weekend. However, there will be little time to rest, with another challenge already on the horizon for Bronze as she prepares to represent England against Greece in a vital two-legged World Cup qualification play-off in October. Bronze is a mainstay under Sarina Wiegman, and speaking before Potter was officially included in the England squad on Tuesday morning, she gave her full support for her Blues team-mate joining the senior ranks. ‘I'm not the manager and Sarina will make her choices, but Lexi has been absolutely fantastic,’ Bronze continued. ‘She was last year too. I remember my first season at Chelsea and seeing her train at the level she was. ‘Having a player like Keira to look up to, and base her style off and learn from, you can see in every game they are developing into the same player. If England have another Keira Walsh, it puts us in a very good position! Similar for Chelsea.’

news.title: OL Lyonnes vs Chelsea Women: How to watch, kick-off time, live stream info
news.body_en: Chelsea Women travel to Lyon for what is set to be a thrilling encounter between two top sides on Wednesday night. The match, which is a one-off fixture as part of the league phase format, will see our head coach Sonia Bompastor face her former side for the first time since joining Chelsea in summer 2024. The reunion doesn't stop there, either. Lucy Bronze, Kadeisha Buchanan, Ellie Carpenter and Melvine Malard all played together for Lyon under Bompastor and assistant coach Camille Abily. Here is everything you need to know about how to watch Chelsea Women against Lyon, including kick-off time and how to follow the action on official Chelsea channels. Chelsea Women's game against Lyon takes place on Wednesday 30 September 2026 at the Parc Olympique Lyonnais, with kick-off scheduled for 8pm UK time. Wednesday night's match will be broadcast live on Disney+ in the UK. In 2019, we were trying to establish ourselves as a force in Europe and came up just short with a 2-1 defeat in the first leg away from home before earning a hard-fought 1-1 draw at Kingsmeadow. By 2023, we had vastly matured as a team, and another thrilling tie against the French giants saw us come away with a thrilling last-gasp win to reach the semi-final of the competition. news.body_en: Five of our Blues have been selected by England head coach Sarina Wiegman for the forthcoming two-legged UEFA Women's European Qualifiers Play-off against Greece. The Lionesses won five of their six group matches earlier in the year, but it wasn't enough to secure an automatic place in the FIFA Women's World Cup in 2027, which will be held in Brazil. England will play Greece over two legs in Round 1 during the October international break. If they come out on top, they will face the winners of Slovakia's tie against Ukraine in Round 2 of the play-offs, which will be contested in late November and early December. Sarina Wiegman's side will travel to the Pankritio Stadium in Heraklion for the first leg on Friday 9 October. The match kicks off at 7.30pm local time, which will be 5.30pm in the UK. The return leg will be held on Tuesday 13 October at the King Power Stadium in Leicester at 7.30pm. Chelsea's experienced England contingent of Lucy Bronze, Hannah Hampton, Lauren James and Keira Walsh have all been selected by Wiegman, and there is also a first call-up for Chelsea Academy graduate Lexi Potter after she has impressed with a string of appearances in our first team. Striker Aggie Beever-Jones is on England's reserve list after recently suffering a small injury and is only just returning to fitness. Potter signed a three-year contract with Chelsea at 17, becoming the first female player to agree a professional deal at this age. She has been part of the England youth setup from Under-17 level onwards, captaining the Under-17 team that reached the semi-finals of the 2023 UEFA European Championships in Estonia. She was also named captain ahead of the 2024 UEFA Euro U19 Championships and once again reached the semi-finals of the competition at Under-19 level. Most recently, Potter was part of the Under-23 side that won the Women's U23 European Competition in April 2026. news.title: Chelsea's Ultimate Goal of the Season: Group D vote
news.body_en: We have reached the final group in our search for Chelsea’s Ultimate Goal of the Season, with five more spectacular strikes competing for the last two places in the quarter-finals. Groups A, B and C have already put 15 previous winners up for the vote, and Group D completes our line-up with goals from Ashley Cole, Lewis Baker, Eden Hazard, Mateo Kovacic and Moises Caicedo. The five contenders cover 14 years of Chelsea history and include everything from brilliant close control inside the penalty area to extraordinary efforts from distance. There is also something unique about this group. Baker’s 2014 winner came for our Under-21s against Arsenal at the Emirates Stadium, making it the only Goal of the Season winner in our 20-goal field which was not scored for the men’s first team. Alongside it are memorable goals at Stamford Bridge and Anfield, including another piece of Hazard magic - incredibly his third entry into this competition, with the previous two having both advanced already. The two goals which receive the most votes will progress to the quarter-finals, completing the eight-goal line-up for the next stage of our Ultimate Goal of the Season contest. You can watch all five Group D contenders below, relive each special moment and choose your favourite by voting on the Chelsea Official App, so make sure you have your say on which strikes deserve to progress. Cast your vote for Group D of our Ultimate Goal of the Season on the Chelsea Official App here Cole raced on to John Terry’s lofted pass, brought the ball under control superbly in the box, cut inside a sliding challenge and then used the outside of his left foot to dink past the keeper and find the far corner during our 7-2 victory over Sunderland. Baker produced an outrageous finish for our Under-21s at the Emirates Stadium, meeting a cross from Islam Feruz first time and improvising brilliantly with a spinning backheel which flew into the Arsenal net, leaving the keeper looking bewildered. Hazard settled a Carabao Cup tie at Anfield in trademark fashion, surging past Naby Keita, nutmegging Alberto Moreno and then firing an unstoppable finish across goal from a tight angle to complete a 2-1 comeback victory. The goal gets better with every rewatch. With the Blues two goals down at Stamford Bridge, Kovacic met a punched clearance from the goalkeeper with a magnificent first-time volley - while moving backwards - from outside the penalty area, sending the ball in off the post to spark our fightback to a 2-2 draw. news.title: Analysis: How Chelsea turned the tide against Arsenal
news.body_en: A big crowd, a fantastic mosaic in the West Stand and plenty of pre-match hype meant that our London derby with Arsenal at Stamford Bridge was hotly anticipated. But for all the pre-match buzz, it was the visitors who had the lion's share of the play in the opening stages, hitting the woodwork twice. For a while, it looked like the Blues were in trouble. But some careful game management, a lot of hard graft and a clinical moment from Alyssa Thompson meant that we came away with three precious points. Here's a look at how we did it... After scoring early in our last two matches, the wins over Birmingham City and Austria Vienna, Chelsea struggled to get hold of the ball against Arsenal. Head coach Sonia Bompastor has often spoken about the advantages of scoring early, explaining that it can serve to kill the opposition's hope early on in a game. Yet Arsenal had 65 per cent possession in the first 15 minutes of Sunday's game, leading many to wonder why we were not able to show the same attacking prowess that we had done in the previous two matches. Of course, it's not easy to dominate a high-level opponent, and that fast start was never guaranteed. If the plan was to let Arsenal have the ball early on, then it was difficult to understand why that would be, especially when we were at home. Bompastor confirmed that Arsenal's early dominance was not part of her tactics. 'We didn't start the way we wanted to,' confirmed the head coach afterwards. 'Our game plan was different from what we did in the first 20 minutes. When we got that break, it was the opportunity for me to adjust and to remind the players what we wanted to do on the pitch. 'We were able to recover that ball, and after that, we capitalised on it. But as much as you tell the players before the game that's what you want, sometimes it doesn't go to plan, and you need to find a way for them to adjust.' Reversing such clear momentum is not an easy task, but that's what Bompastor helped her players to do, and in the first 15 minutes of the second half, we enjoyed 72 per cent of the ball. Lucy Bronze has proven that she thrives in high-pressure moments, and has even discussed how she can raise her level when it matters in previous interviews. A home game against rivals Arsenal was one of those occasions for the experienced defender, and a look at her numbers shows how she led by example while wearing the captain's armband. Bronze won five of her six attempted tackles, the most of any Chelsea player on the day. She also made two blocks, won three aerial duels and recovered the ball on five occasions. Not only content to carry out her defensive duties against a quality opponent, she made 16 passes in the final third of the pitch, created one chance and took a shot at goal. It was a trademark battling display from the 34-year-old, and one that certainly helped us secure the win on Sunday. Chelsea Academy graduate Lexi Potter has been playing more minutes this season, and developing an increasingly effective partnership with Keira Walsh. But few would've expected the youngster to be named in the starting line-up against Arsenal, with games of this magnitude often reserved for players with more experience. Bompastor showed how highly she values the youngster by placing her in the XI to start against the Gunners, and explained afterwards why she did so. 'For her age, being able to be consistent in the way she's been performing is great,' said the head coach. 'Probably people were also looking forward to this game to see if, on this big occasion, she was able to repeat and sustain the performance, and she proved that today.' It's not only her own performances that have secured a place in the side for Potter. Her reliability in the deeper midfield slot is allowing Walsh to express her qualities more in attack, as Bompastor also explained. 'Keira is playing at that level because she has more freedom to go forward, because she has Lexi next to her. When Keira is at that level, she's the boss on the pitch.' The graphic above shows how many of Walsh's touches are outside of the centre circle. And when compared to Potter's touch map below, it's clear that the 20-year-old is covering that central area in place of Walsh, allowing her counterpart to make a difference in attack. It's something that Walsh herself spoke about after the Arsenal victory. 'Last year I sometimes let games pass by without having much impact, and that's something I've focused on this season,' said Walsh after the match. 'Having Lexi behind allows me to do that.' It was a tough job to stay high up the pitch against Arsenal, but someone had to do it. The average position graphic below demonstrates how Chelsea were much less positionally aggressive against the Gunners than we have been in other matches this season. Some of that can be put down to playing an opponent who can be extremely dangerous on the counter-attack, but as discussed earlier, much of it was down to those early minutes of domination from the visitors. Up top was Melvine Malard, holding the line, battling for possession and being ready for any out ball that might've come her way. Playing the central striker role isn't always glamorous, but our summer signing has shown she is willing to do the hard work for the team. Taking five shots, two of which were on target, she also completed all eight of her passes in the final third, while winning the ball back twice and completing both of her attempted tackles. This was a clear indication of Malard's value to the team even on a day when she wasn't on the scoresheet.

news.title: Training gallery: Back to work!
Katie McCabe on playing smart and 'riding the storms' against former club Arsenal
news.body_en: Katie McCabe knows only too well the strengths of her former side, and that was exactly why she was delighted to seal the win against Arsenal at Stamford Bridge on Sunday afternoon. The Ireland captain made the move across London in the summer in search of a fresh challenge after ten years with the Gunners. And while others talked at length about her return to face them for the first time since that exit, McCabe was focused exclusively on helping earn three points for Chelsea. ‘For me it was all about us and our preparation going into the game,’ she said. ‘Obviously, we know Arsenal pose a lot of threats, and they've got a lot of quality on the ball and around the box, but it was up to us to ride the storm a little bit in the first half. ‘But once we settled in, got control of the ball, we dominated in periods and Alyssa (Thompson) took our goal really well. ‘As I said, Arsenal are a fantastic footballing team, and they're going to dominate at times, but it's what we do without the ball and how we can control the spaces. ‘And in the first part of the first half, we did it really well. In the second half, they changed formation; they put on a lot of attackers, so they were chasing the game, and we needed to stick together and grind out the result. ‘We got up the pitch, kept the ball in the corner, and sometimes it's just about playing smart. We did that and picked up the three points.’ The Arsenal fans, tucked in the corner at the far side of the East Stand, made their feelings known whenever McCabe touched the ball. But for an experienced professional, the reception is an ordinary part of playing football and will not taint her memories of the past. ‘Having been with the club for so long, it's expected, especially going to a London rival,' she explained. 'But I have a lot of respect for the Arsenal fans. ‘We've been through a lot together, but for me, it was time for a new chapter in my career. I was really excited to come to Chelsea with the way Sonia wants to play and the quality we have in the team. ‘I'm delighted with the win, and that's most important.’ Keira Walsh had plenty of positive words to say about her Irish team-mate in her post-match interview, and McCabe duly returned those compliments with some praise of her own. ‘We absolutely controlled everything in the midfield, and credit to Keira as always,' McCabe smiled. ‘I've played against her for so long. We’ve known each other a long time. Back in the Man City, Arsenal days, which are what… ten years ago now? I always heard the English girls coming back from camp saying, "Oh, Keira's in the team, Keira's in the team," and what she offers. ‘But actually playing with her means when I give her the ball under pressure, she brings calmness and composure. She doesn't lose the ball. ‘I don't want to jinx her now, but you can't get the ball off her, and I think she's just always five steps ahead of everyone else with her vision. I like to play through the lines - Keira's always an option for me. I trust her in those tight spaces, and she can score, too!’

news.title: WSL Full Match: Chelsea Women vs Arsenal Women
Keira Walsh on 'outfighting' Arsenal and 'exceptional talent' Lexi Potter
news.body_en: Keira Walsh reflected on the victory over Arsenal after another standout individual performance and explained exactly what this Chelsea side has added to our game to make us more difficult to beat this season. We have kept a clean sheet in our last three matches and only conceded three goals in our opening seven games of the season in all competitions. And while this side has always possessed the technical skill to dominate matches, Walsh thinks the difference-maker this season has been the team’s work rate and willingness to fight for each other. ‘It’s great to win any game, even if it wasn't Arsenal,’ the midfielder explained. ‘But they're a top team, and it made it a little bit more special that it was a home derby. ‘It was difficult for us, but we controlled the game for large parts of it. Then at the end, when it came to managing the game a little bit – because they were throwing loads of attackers on – defending our box and keeping a clean sheet was really important. ‘It was probably the best we've built up [this season]. We were really comfortable on the ball when we had it, especially after the first 20 minutes. We really settled down and grew into the game. ‘Probably it would’ve been better to start the game a little bit quicker. Last season maybe Arsenal probably would've scored then and it could’ve been 2-0 or 3-0. That's probably the difference this year, and I think we've got both sides to our game now. ‘We can control the ball, and we are also a lot more difficult to beat,' added Walsh. 'We're really tight defending our box now. Obviously, we know we can play with the ball, but maybe we can outwork and outfight teams. That's been something else we’ve been doing as well, and that really helped. ‘We do it as a team rather than individuals, and this year, we know we've got each other's backs. We're working for each other. If a ball goes past me, I know Lex (Lexi Potter) is there clearing up. We all work together and that's probably been the most important so far this season.’ Walsh and Potter have formed quite the duo in midfield this season. Head coach Sonia Bompastor showed her faith in the young Chelsea Academy graduate by handing her a starting berth in the London derby alongside her vastly more experienced counterpart. There may be a mismatch in terms of minutes played, but as Walsh explained, Potter is fitting in perfectly in the first team and has a bright future ahead of her. ‘Lexi is really intelligent,’ Walsh said. ‘She makes me feel really comfortable when I'm playing next to her. The way she sees the game, there aren't many female players who understand it the way she does. ‘She's an exceptional talent, and she plays beyond her years. She's got a very calm head on her shoulders, and she's got a lot more to come, I think. She’s going to be an incredible player for Chelsea and England in the future.’ Walsh chose to single out another of her team-mates in her post-match comments, praising Katie McCabe for the contribution she has made to the side on and off the pitch since her summer transfer from cross-city rivals Arsenal. Another player may have shrunk under the pressure of facing her former side, especially in the face of a largely hostile reception from the contingent of visiting supporters at Stamford Bridge. Yet McCabe stood tall and delivered another outstanding performance in blue, and it didn't go unnoticed. 'I think Katie coming to us has added an extra edge, and her physicality and mentality really ramp it up,' said Walsh. 'Every time she does a little team talk, we play quite well, so hopefully that continues. She's fitted in really well. 'I'm not surprised she handled the atmosphere, to be honest. That's the sort of player she is. She works hard every day; she wants to win every single part of every training session. I think we needed that a little bit more last year, and she's definitely brought that. I’ve enjoyed every minute playing with her. 'She's really smart; she’s got a great left foot as well, so she's brought a massive part to our team. She's just so passionate about the game and you can really feel it when she's speaking. It gets the players going and definitely gets me going, so it’s great if she keeps doing it.'

news.title: WNL Cup report: Maidenhead United 0-1 Chelsea Women Under-18s
news.body_en: Chelsea Women's Under-18s secured top spot in our Women's National League Cup group with a 1-0 win away at Maidenhead United, with Stevie Sinclair grabbing a 90th-minute winner. The Blues, who play in the PGA Under-21 Women's League and cup competition, had 74 per cent of possession but found it difficult to create clear chances in the first half against Maidenhead's 5-4-1 low block. Sadie Gregory hit the post during that spell. Chelsea had 13 shots after the interval, six of them on target. Maidenhead goalkeeper Cherry Priesner made important saves to deny Chelsea N'Drin and Nelly Las before substitute Sinclair struck late on. First team players Lola Brown, Las, and Chloe Sarwie featured for Leanne Champ's side for the first time this season. Chelsea had most of the ball from the start but were limited to efforts from distance and half-chances as Maidenhead defended deep. The closest we came in the first half was on 20 minutes. The ball was worked out from the right-hand side of the box to Gregory, and the centre-back stepped in and struck a curling left-footed shot that hit the left post. Ten minutes later, Las picked out her fellow wing-back Sarwie at the back post, but Sarwie narrowly missed the target with a flying volley. The Blues had five shots in the first half, none of which were on target, and the game was goalless at half-time. Champ made three changes at the break, bringing on Rebekah Pierce, Tess Finn and Sinclair for Gregory, Keira Johnson and Jahmya Putman. Chelsea were more threatening after the restart. On 64 minutes, Elise Christian replaced Annie Boichat. A minute later, N'Drin looked set to score after a failed clearance, but Priesner grasped the ball before it crossed the line. The Maidenhead goalkeeper denied Chelsea again on 76 minutes. Captain Belle Sullivan (pictured top) won the ball back high up the pitch, and Finn laid it off to Las on the edge of the box. Las struck across goal, but Priesner stopped the shot before it could go in. The breakthrough came in the 90th minute. Sinclair won the first contact from a Maidenhead goal kick, and after a battle for the loose ball in midfield, it broke to Brown with space to drive forward. Brown played the ball out to Pierce, who took on her defender one-on-one before playing a reverse pass to Las on the top left corner of the box. Las drove into the area and picked out Sinclair on the penalty spot, and she curled a left-footed shot into the top corner. It was Sinclair's third goal in the WNL Cup this season and her eighth in all competitions. A draw would have been enough for Chelsea to top the group, but the win means we ,finish on nine points, ahead of Tier 3 side Swindon Town on six, Tier 4 side Maidenhead on three and Wycombe Wanderers on zero. Chelsea move into the WNL Cup knockout stages, which is where our run ended last season. We were the only academy side to progress from the groups last term, and this season the Blues will be looking for a competitive draw and the chance to go further than any academy side has before. After a ten-day break, Chelsea begin our PGA Cup campaign at home against West Ham United Women Under-21s in the preliminary qualification round on Wednesday 7 October. The Blues then start the PGA National Division One season on Wednesday 18 November. We qualified after topping the Southern phase and finishing with the best record across the North and South divisions. Chelsea Diary: European test, London derby and international action
news.body_en: A big week lies ahead for Chelsea Women, with a Champions League trip to France followed by a London derby against West Ham. news.title: WSL Highlights: Chelsea Women 1-0 Arsenal Women
Internationals: Neto assists Portugal to victory
news.body_en: Pedro Neto created a goal for his former Chelsea team-mate Joao Felix as Portugal recorded an impressive 2-1 win away to Norway in the UEFA Nations League on Sunday evening. Neto played 87 minutes in Oslo and set up the opener after dribbling down the left wing and intelligently laying the ball into the path of Joao Felix, located on the edge of the box. He took a touch and finished with aplomb. That 16th-minute goal was cancelled out by Erling Haaland early in the second half, but Goncalo Ramos restored Portugal’s lead soon after following an error by Orjan Nyland. Ramos then thought he had scored a second, but a lengthy VAR checked showed there had been an offside in the build-up. Norway pressed for a second equaliser late on during an entertaining encounter, but the Portuguese stood firm to make it two wins from two as they seek to defend the Nations League crown they won last summer. Neto was replaced by Bernardo Silva three minutes from time. Elsewhere at senior level, Jorrel Hato was an unused substitute as the Netherlands beat Serbia 2-1 in Belgrade. Earlier on Sunday, four Chelsea players featured for England Under-18s as they qualified for the semi-finals of the UEFA Friendship Cup with a 2-1 win over Egypt in Nyon. Ryan Kavuma-McQueen, who is spending the season on loan at Portsmouth, opened the scoring on the quarter-hour with a superb strike from 20 yards out. The winger carried a threat throughout the first half, forcing a good save from the opposition goalkeeper following another mazy run and flashing an angled drive inches wide of the far post. Gabriel Sambou and Jashayde Greenwood were introduced midway through the second half, while Calvin Diakite also entered the fray, with Kavuma-McQueen one of those to make way. Egypt levelled with 11 minutes left but the Young Lions were soon back in front and it was Greenwood who supplied the precise pass that set up Michael Mills of Newcastle to score the winning goal. England Under-18s next play on Wednesday 30 September against South Korea.

news.title: 'The fans gave the team the boost they needed'
Sonia Bompastor on Lauren James' fitness and being 'strong and together' after Arsenal win
news.body_en: Sonia Bompastor explained why Lauren James was substituted after 60 minutes of our 1-0 win over Arsenal and reflected on how the Blues were able to pull together to secure the three points. After a strong start to the game from the visitors, the Blues wrestled back momentum, taking the lead through Alyssa Thompson's strike on 39 minutes. Yet there was plenty of work still to be done as both sides exchanged chances in the second half. Chelsea dug deep to secure the three points, spurred on by the Blues fans who made themselves heard in what was an electric atmosphere inside Stamford Bridge. After grinding out a 1-0 victory against Austria Vienna in midweek, we recorded another hard-fought win against our London rivals, and the head coach explained that the tenacity shown by her players so far this season is something that the team has been working hard on behind the scenes. 'The plan for us this season is mindset and mentality,' explained Bompastor. 'I've been talking a lot about being strong and being together. No matter what happens in the game, I always want to see a group of players, and also a team who is together in our high moments when we doing well, but also in the low moments. 'We came into this game well-prepared in terms of knowing we were going to have some moments in the game where we were probably not in control, especially in possession of the ball, because we knew how good Arsenal are at doing that. 'So we prepared the game for those moments. Even if we didn't have the ball, we knew exactly where we wanted to rotate the ball and where we wanted to leave some spaces, and I think we dealt with that really well. 'We were also really strong in terms of the mental aspect, but also physical aspects: winning the duels and defending the box. To not concede against an Arsenal side who are a strong team with great talent in the attacking line, midfield, the fullbacks...everywhere, it's a great result and performance.' The win against Arsenal was our fourth consecutive clean sheet in all competitions. The Blues have only conceded three times in seven matches this season: two in our first fixture against Real Sociedad, and once against Aston Villa at Stamford Bridge. The head coach is pleased with our defensive performances, and with another big test to come away at Lyon on Wednesday night, the head coach explained how she would reflect on what can be learned from the latest win. 'I'm pleased with the effort the players put on the pitch today,' she continued.  'From the beginning of the season, we didn't concede a lot of goals, which is great. I'm pleased with that. 'We still have some work to be done in those areas, and then we'll reflect on the game and take the learnings. But I think it was a strong performance today in terms of the out-of-possession work.' After missing last Wednesday's match against Austria Vienna, Lauren James returned to the starting line-up today, but was withdrawn after an hour. Bompastor gave an update on her condition and explained why she was substituted. 'We knew after LJ got a knock in training, we didn't want to take any risks because this game was coming,' she said. 'Sometimes what is difficult for a head coach is that every game is important because when you think about rotating and managing the squad, you need to make sure you mainly win the games. 'With the information from the medical team from the beginning, I knew we were going to prepare for LJ to start this game, and it was great news. Having 60 minutes was probably a good plan because she hadn't played for one week. 'She didn't stay home for a long time, but I think maybe she still couldn't work the way she would have liked to. So 60 minutes was good, and she brought a contribution to the game.'

news.title: 'It feels amazing'
Match gallery: Blues triumph in London derby!
Match report: Chelsea 1-0 Arsenal
news.body_en: A superb strike from Alyssa Thompson and a battling second-half display earned us a 1-0 victory over Arsenal at Stamford Bridge in the London derby on Sunday afternoon. This was undoubtedly a big occasion at the Bridge. The fans in the West Stand held their cards aloft to spell out the word 'Blues' ahead of kick-off, and both sets of fans raised their voices in support of their respective sides. The Gunners took control in the opening stages of the game, hitting the woodwork twice as they dominated possession. But we played patiently and gradually got ourselves back into the contest before an emphatic finish from Thompson put us 1-0 up before half-time, to the delight of the home supporters. The second half saw both teams exchange chances; however, we pulled together strongly and, helped by our fans, saw out the victory to take all three points against our rivals at the Bridge. Sonia Bompastor made four alterations to her starting line-up from the side that recorded a 1-0 win over Austria Vienna in midweek. Livia Peng, Sandy Baltimore, Veerle Buurman and Sjoeke Nusken made way for Hannah Hampton, Lucy Bronze, Lauren James and Lexi Potter. Bronze took the captain's armband for the afternoon, and a fit-again Aggie Beever-Jones was named on the bench. The visitors dominated possession in the opening 15 minutes, taking four shots on goal, but they failed to threaten Hampton with any real penetration or attempts on target. That was until Gunners captain Kim Little got a fraction in front of Buchanan on the right-hand side of the penalty area and pulled the trigger, striking the woodwork with her effort from a tight angle. Then came our first real chance of the game when Ellie Carpenter put in a dangerous ball on the right that Wieke Kaptein couldn't quite reach. The ball fell to Melvine Malard, but a crowd of Arsenal players prevented her getting any clean contact on a shot. Renee Slegers' side made a quick breakaway straight after that chance, and the ball fell to Mariona Caldentey in acres of space. Her shot crashed against the near post, but it looked like Hampton had it covered. From that point, the Blues slowly gained a foothold into the game, increasing our possession of the ball and looking much more assured. Just as it was looking like the teams would head into the break all square, a brilliant passage of play gave us the advantage. Arsenal attempted to play out from the back from a goal kick, and the Blues were alive with our press as Wieke Kaptein intercepted the ball, finding Carpenter. The Australian evaded a tackle before Malard laid it off to Keira Walsh, who took a shot from the edge of the penalty area. When goalkeeper Anneke Borbe could only parry, Thompson seized her opportunity to take hold of the ball and fired in with power from the left corner of the six-yard box. We could've even had two before the break. Carpenter played a long ball down the channel to Malard. The No. 9 sprinted into the box, forcing a save from Borbe and winning a Chelsea corner. The second half began with a looping cross into the box from James, and as Borbe spilt the ball, Malard was almost there to net the rebound, but the offside flag stopped any chance of us doubling our advantage. Hampton was called into action shortly afterwards to deny a shot from Lisa Baum, the England international getting down well to keep out a strike with plenty of power. Malard went close again just after the hour mark, receiving a pass from Bronze on the edge of the box before her shot rolled agonisingly wide of the far post. Both sides continued to have chances as substitute Nusken nearly scored with her first touch, beating Leah Williamson but seeing her chance extinguished by the onrushing Borbe. Up at the other end, Katie McCabe made a crucial block on a shot from Arsenal substitute Chloe Kelly. As the minutes ticked down towards full time, the tension was high inside Stamford Bridge. Steph Catley whipped in a corner, which was punched away by Hampton and hacked clear by Sandy Baltimore. Arsenal were determined to throw the kitchen sink at us in an attempt to snatch a late equaliser. The referee indicated there would be five minutes remaining and there was a gasp around Stamford Bridge. Carpenter then ran the length of the pitch to put a cross into the box, but in the end, there was no one to meet it. Yet this helped to ease the pressure on the Blues just a little, as we ran the clock down by keeping the ball down that right-hand flank, and ultimately saw out the win with complete professionalism. The win leaves us just two points behind Women's Super League leaders Manchester City, with an away league fixture against West Ham United to come next Sunday 4 October. We travel to Bompastor's former side Lyon as we take on the French champions in the league phase of the Women's Champions League on Wednesday evening. news.title: Millie | A CFCW film 🎥
Millie Bright's incredible Chelsea tenure celebrated in behind-the-scenes exclusive documentary
news.body_en: Millie, an exclusive documentary celebrating the storied career of our former captain, Millie Bright, is now streaming on the Chelsea Official app and website! Bright retired from football in April after 12 unforgettable years at Chelsea. With 314 appearances and a place in the side for all 20 major trophies won in our history, her legacy will continue far beyond her playing days. She is the first women's team player to be immortalised on the Shed Wall, while the sensory room at Stamford Bridge is now named in her honour to mark the work she has done off the pitch, which she will continue after being named a Chelsea Foundation trustee. The documentary goes behind the scenes at her family home in Killamarsh, talking to her grassroots coaches and the Bright family about how she began her football journey as a child. It is available to watch in full below. Bright recounts some of the most personal moments of her incredible Chelsea career, discusses her winning mentality and talks with honesty about the reasons behind her decision to retire from football. The former Blues captain's career trajectory ran parallel to the growth of women's football, and she saw firsthand how the popularity of the Women's Super League exploded after she was part of England's Women's European Championship-winning side in 2022. 'I went in as one person, came out as something completely different,' she told us when she announced her retirement. 'It was the most overwhelming situation I've ever been in. I just didn't know what to do with myself. I didn't leave the house for six days!' There's also a look inside her passion for helping others and inspiring the next generation of footballers, as one of the most experienced voices in the women's game. This is a chance for Blues fans to get to know the person who lies underneath all the trophies and the success, and what drove her to reach those heights. The full in-depth documentary is available to watch exclusively on the Chelsea Official App and website - just make sure you are signed in!

news.title: Chelsea's Ultimate Goal of the Season: Group C vote
news.body_en: The search for Chelsea’s Ultimate Goal of the Season moves on to Group C, with another five memorable strikes competing for your votes! Groups A and B have already brought together the first 10 winners in our 20-goal contest and now it is the turn of Michael Essien, Ramires and Eden Hazard, all for the second time in this competition, as well as Olivier Giroud and Conor Gallagher. This group stretches from 2009 to 2023 and includes goals scored on some huge occasions, from UEFA Champions League knockout nights to dramatic Premier League encounters. There is plenty of quality to choose from, too. A stunning volley off the crossbar, a mazy individual run, an overhead kick and a last-minute winner all feature in Group C. The two goals which receive the most votes will advance to the quarter-finals, as we continue to narrow down our 20 Goal of the Season winners along the road to finding the ultimate winner. You can watch all five Group C contenders below, relive each special moment and choose your favourite by voting on the Chelsea Official App, so make sure you have your say on which strikes deserve to progress. Cast your vote for our Ultimate Goal of the Season on the Chelsea Official App here On a huge Champions League night at Stamford Bridge, Essien met a looping ball outside the penalty area with a magnificent left-footed volley, which crashed in off the underside of the crossbar to give us the lead against Barcelona. Ramires showcased the full extent of his skill and dribbling ability against Man City, weaving his way between defenders just outside the penalty area before bearing down on goal and firing beyond Joe Hart to round off a 2-0 victory at the Bridge. One of Hazard’s most memorable moments in Chelsea blue. Picking up possession inside his own half, Eden powered away from the Arsenal midfield, shrugged off Francis Coquelin and continued into the box before calmly beating Petr Cech to complete a sensational solo goal. Giroud produced a spectacular moment in our Champions League last-16 first leg against Atletico, adjusting brilliantly from 12 yards to send an overhead kick beyond Jan Oblak and secure a valuable victory on our way to lifting the Champions League trophy for the second time. Against the club where he had spent the previous season on loan, Gallagher marked his first Chelsea goal in style. First he nutmegged Jean-Philippe Mateta, before curling a brilliant effort into the top corner from outside the box in the 90th minute, to seal a 2-1 victory at Selhurst Park. news.title: Ellie Carpenter on a 'massive rivalry', revenge and a sea of blue
news.body_en: Ellie Carpenter now has enough experience at Chelsea to know that our contests against Arsenal are always high stakes. In the WSL last season - Carpenter's first in blue - we drew at the Emirates Stadium before losing at home to our rivals. Then came a two-legged knockout clash in the Women’s Champions League quarter-final. With the atmosphere at fever pitch in both legs, the Gunners took a 3-1 lead into the decisive leg back in SW6, despite a closely-fought battle. The season before we had overturned a two-goal deficit against Manchester City at the Bridge in the UWCL quarter-final, securing a famous 3-0 victory. The whole stadium believed we could do the same again against Arsenal. A superb performance followed, but Sjoeke Nusken's late goal wasn't enough for us to advance. That’s where Carpenter picks up the story as we prepare to take on Arsenal at the Bridge once more, this time in the Women’s Super League. ‘It's a massive rivalry,’ she tells us. ‘Even before I joined the club, I remember I would always watch Arsenal against Chelsea. It's just one you'd want to put on TV. It’s always a good match, and always a high-tempo game with lots of things happening. It’s probably the biggest rivalry in the league. ‘None of us will ever forget that second leg against Arsenal, because of how well we played and also beating them as well. I guess we still want that bit of revenge for not going through to the semi-final of the Champions League. I'm sure that's in the back of our minds as well. ‘Arsenal are a great team, they have great players, and I'm sure they'll be up for the game. They’ve not been winning their recent matches in the league, so I'm sure they'll be hungry to get more points. It'll be a big game, so we'll have to turn up, and everyone will have to be at their best to win.’ Renee Slegers’ side have scored just twice in their opening three WSL games. After a 1-0 win over Brighton and Hove Albion, and a goalless draw with newly-promoted Crystal Palace, they needed a last-minute goal to grab a point against Manchester United. Yet as Carpenter explains, the team is unconcerned with any previous form, especially as the level of competition in the league is constantly increasing. ‘For us, we just need to focus on ourselves and play the football that we've been playing this season,’ she continued. ‘I think we've had really great performances in all three games. Now it's just about finishing off all the chances we're creating. We just need to keep playing our game plan. ‘Every game is big in the WSL. Right now is probably the strongest the league has ever been. Anyone can win on any given day. Anyone can take points from anyone, and that's what's so good about this league. ‘It's so competitive, and you have to be at your best every weekend to get the three points. That's why I think it's the best league in the world.’ Carpenter has been in top form so far this season. She earned the Player of the Match trophy against Birmingham City, and was also voted Star of the Match for her performance that day by our own supporters. Ahead of one of the biggest tests of the season, the Australian explained why she is revelling in the challenge of playing at the highest level for the Blues. ‘It’s why I wanted to move to England, for sure,’ she says. ‘To play for Chelsea is to play in the best league and to be tested every weekend. Not just against Arsenal, but every weekend it's a test, and you have to bring your best game to get the three points. ‘That’s what I'm enjoying about this league: the expectation and also the pressure to perform. It’s really helped me personally to grow as a footballer on the pitch. ‘I've had a good pre-season with the team, and I guess I'm in a more attacking role these first couple of matches, so it's been nice to get forward and probably more on the attack.’ We have declared the fixture against Arsenal a ‘Blue Day’, meaning there will be special events happening in and around the ground so that our supporters can show their allegiance in a very visual way on Sunday. Answer Ellie's call and get your tickets for Arsenal at the Bridge! Fans are being encouraged to wear Chelsea blue, bring their scarves and wave the flags that will be left on the seats. For those in the West Lower, there will be cards provided to make a mosaic as the teams walk out. And as the derby takes place during a break in men’s fixtures for internationals, it’s the ideal time for all Chelsea fans to show that London is blue. Ellie agrees. ‘It'll be good to see a sea of blue in the stands,’ she says. ‘Hopefully not many red shirts! It'll be nice to see Stamford Bridge full of blue, cheering for us, and hopefully we’ll get a great crowd.’ You can still attend today's huge London derby clash, with kick-off at the Bridge at 4.30pm!

news.title: From the archive: Peter Bonetti on the 1970 FA Cup final
news.body_en: On what would have been his 85th birthday, we look back to when the late, great Peter Bonetti shared his account of one of his greatest moments at Chelsea, our maiden FA Cup triumph in 1970. In the eyes of many, Bonetti - who sadly passed away in 2020 - is regarded as Chelsea's most legendary goalkeeper, and one of the greatest of his incredible 729 games for the Blues was reserved for the biggest of stages. In the FA Cup final of 1969/70, ‘the Cat’ was bright, brave and brilliant across two hours of high-octane, high-stakes football. He made some truly spectacular saves in the first game at Wembley and was our stand-out player as Dave Sexton’s side twice came from behind to force a replay. Up at Old Trafford a fortnight later, with a record TV audience of over 28 million watching at home, Bonetti’s efforts were superhuman as he battled through an early injury to defy Leeds United as our last line of defence. Although it was feline agility and reflexes that earned him his nickname, it was the heart of a lion in Manchester that saw him soldier on through another period of extra time, during which David Webb bundled in that famous winner to ensure the Blues were FA Cup victors for the very first time in our history. Those who watched at the time recall it as one of the most memorable goalkeeping performances in FA Cup final history, while the man who wore the gloves remembers it as the most physical game of his career. ‘They’re two of the most important games, as far as I’m concerned, in Chelsea’s history,’ Bonetti told us in 2010. ‘My memories of the FA Cup final are fantastic and obviously the games were quite exceptional too. ‘It was between two teams that didn’t really like one another and so it was obviously going to be a very physical battle between the two. I’d say that the replay at Old Trafford was the most physical game I ever played in. ‘I wasn’t necessarily referring to the Mick Jones incident where he banged into my knee because that sort of thing can happen – you go up and try to catch a ball and someone challenges you. His knee caught my knee and I don’t think it was deliberate. ‘So I didn’t just mean it was physical because of that, but both teams were so desperate to win because they didn’t like one another at the time. And I must say "at the time" because it’s a bit different today! ‘If the game had been refereed according to the rules and regulations of today, it wouldn’t have lasted! The tackling was wild, you had people kicking each other six foot in the air and trying to kick the ball as someone headed it! ‘But that was the way the game was played in those days, it was very physical. You were out to win, just like nowadays, but it was played in a more aggressive manner, I must admit.’ Bonetti felt it was the Chelsea character that proved the difference between two well-matched teams and speculated on what might have been had his own Herculean effort proved insufficient to keep him on the field after that first-half knee injury. A collision with Leeds centre-forward Jones had done the damage, leaving the Chelsea No1 struggling to even walk properly and requiring a pain-killing injection at half-time. At a time before substitute goalkeepers had been introduced to the game, there was a chance that the eventual match-winner could have had an altogether different role to play. ‘We showed great character over the two games,’ continued Bonetti. ‘I think we were behind three times and got back each time before Webby got the winner. It showed we had great character as a team and a tremendous blend of players. ‘We weren’t surprised when Webby got the goal. He was a great character who was fearless – he’d go up for set-pieces and just throw himself at everything. And he was a very recognised goal scorer too. He scored in the quarter-final and semi-final that year, and I remember him scoring three goals in a Boxing Day match at Ipswich once. He had the eye for a goal, no doubt about it. ‘If my knee injury had kept me out of the game then he’d have been the one to go in goal! If I got injured, he used to go in goal.’ The Cat was voted runner-up in the Footballer of the Year award at the end of that campaign, his FA Cup winners’ medal alongside others in the League Cup, European Cup Winners’ Cup and, of course, the FIFA World Cup. After hanging up his gloves in 1986, it was those medals that ultimately provided most pride to Bonetti. ‘It was the first time the club had ever won the FA Cup and the other thing was that it meant we won medals,' he concluded. ‘You always look back on your career at times when you have won something and there’s so many players who go through their careers without winning anything. So I regard myself as being lucky at having been able to win a couple of things.’ For the supporters who watched him at Stamford Bridge in his prime, it was certainly the Blues who were the lucky ones, for being able to count on Bonetti between the posts during an unbelievable Chelsea career spanning 20 years.
